label: <DEL> step of long (L>=8) sequences, rare token-dependent subset
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L), and almost only when L is 8 or 9 (98% of activations and mass; 6 hits at L=7, none for L<=6). It never fires in the original or copy phases. Even within that context it is very sparse: about 0.7% of L=8 and 1.5% of L=9 delimiter steps, so the location predicate has ~1% precision. Which long sequences trigger it depends on token content in a diffuse way. It is enriched when the first original token (the one about to be output) is f, z, 1 or e (f alone gives 28% of mass), when the last original token is e/u/v/j, and when the second original token is a digit or z/f/x. Adding these lists raises precision only to ~4-13% and costs recall, so the selection rule is not captured. Activations are tiny (max 0.035 above threshold). Magnitude was not seen to depend on any variable checked beyond those enrichments.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=e (+3.33), phase=1 & out_tok=f (+3.17), prev_tok=u (+2.56), prev_tok=v (+2.52), prev_tok=j (+2.28), orig3=z (+2.19). Lower it: in_first=0 (-4.76), orig7=- (-3.72), orig6=- (-2.10), in_count=1 (-2.06).
